sources.title: Pyotr Semyonov-Tyan-Shansky (Q326010), verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-11-06): English label 'Pyotr Semyonov-Tyan-Shansky', description 'Russian geographer, art collector and statistician', Korean label 표트르 세묘노프탼샨스키, born 1827-01-02 and died 1914-02-26 (Julian-calendar dates; the Gregorian dates are 14 January 1827 and 11 March 1914), citizenship Russian Empire. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Dictionary of Scientific Biography entry 'Semyonov-Tyan-Shansky, Petr Petrovich' (Gale, reproduced on Encyclopedia.com; read in full including its bibliography). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Tien Shan expedition of 1856-57 (refuted Humboldt's volcanic theory and the Chu-Issyk-Kul link, found extensive glaciation, drew the first orographic scheme), translation and expansion of Ritter's Asia volumes, five-volume Geographical-Statistical Dictionary 1863-85, head of the Central Statistical Committee from 1864, First All-Russian Statistical Congress 1870, 1897 census, vice-president of the Russian Geographical Society from 1873 and organiser of the Przhevalsky, Pevtsov, Potanin, Kozlov and Obruchev expeditions, a Dutch-painting collection and a 700,000-specimen insect collection. Reference-work biography, admiring in tone; it states the 1906 'Tyan-Shansky' addition as a 'fiftieth' anniversary in one place and 'fifteenth' in another, and says the painting collection was 'presented' to the Hermitage in 1910, which the Sokolova review contradicts (offered for sale at half its value; passed to the Hermitage after his death in 1914).

L. I. Sumarokov, 'How the Siberian artist Pavel Kosharov preserved the historical image of the Kyrgyz people', Vestnik KRSU 26(2), 2026, pp. 32-40 (Kyrgyz-Russian Slavic University; Russian-language scholarly article, read in full in the PDF). Reports the Russian Geographical Society's 1857 annual report on the expedition (23 passes explored, more than 300 rock samples and about 1,000 plants), the 23 November 1906 imperial decree adding 'Tyan-Shansky' to the surname, Semyonov's choice of an expedition artist and his appraisal of him, and a quoted letter to his sister on the loss of two horses at the Dzhuuk pass. Admiring, focused on the artist; Semyonov's own letters and memoirs are quoted (self-report).

Historians of Netherlandish Art, review of Irina Sokolova, 'The Russian Passion for Dutch Painting of the Golden Age: The Collection of Pyotr Semenov and the Art Market in St. Petersburg, 1860-1910' (Brill, 2015) (review read in full). Independent art-history voice: the collection reached over 700 paintings, built on a modest income through small masters and signed works, bought in St Petersburg and at Frederik Muller in Amsterdam; friendships with Bode, Bredius and Hofstede de Groot; his 1906 catalogue and the Etudes volume; in 1910 he offered the whole collection (with more than 3,000 prints) to the Hermitage at half its appraised value so it would stay together, and it passed to the Hermitage on his death in 1914; more than 220 of the 700 paintings were later sold abroad by the Soviet state. Also describes him as politically a liberal tied to the campaign to end serfdom (context only, not scored).

EBSCO Research Starters, 'Przhevalsky explores Central Asia' (opened through a summarising fetch tool, so the full text was not read line by line). Presents Semenov as head of the quasi-governmental Russian Geographical Society who wanted to build on his own Tian Shan work, helped fund Przhevalsky's 1871 expedition with the War Department, held that accurate physical-geographical knowledge and a census were keys to a modern state, and notes that Soviet-era writers stressed his contributions while downplaying Przhevalsky. Independent framing from the Przhevalsky side; summary-level only.

Saint Petersburg Encyclopaedia (encspb.ru), entry 'Semenov-Tyan-Shansky P.P., (1827-1914), geographer' by L. I. Yarukova (read in full): graduated 1848; 1856-57 Tien Shan journey and first reliable data on the range; 1864-73 head of the Central Statistical Committee; initiated and organised the 1897 census; vice-president of the Russian Geographical Society 1873-1914 and head of the Russian Entomological Society 1890-1914; the Geographical-Statistical Dictionary (1863-85), Picturesque Russia and the multi-author geographical description of Russia. City reference work; celebratory and brief.

Moscow city 'Historical patriotic navigation' page for Semenov-Tyan-Shansky Street (read in full): Tien Shan journey 1856-57 across the Altai, Tarbagatai, Alatau ranges, Khan Tengri and Issyk-Kul; 1888 journey to Turkestan and the Transcaspian region; three-volume history of the Russian Geographical Society; the Society's Semenov gold medal; son Veniamin's continuation of the geographical description of Russia. Municipal commemorative page; celebratory, used only for consistent factual dates.

Andriy Posunko, review of Andreyev, Baskhanov and Yusupova, 'The Quest for Forbidden Lands: Nikolai Przhevalskii and His Followers on Inner Asian Tracks' (Brill, 2017), Ab Imperio 2/2019 (Project MUSE, review text read). CONTEXT AND COUNTER-VOICE: frames Russian exploration of Inner Asia as sponsored by military, scholarly and private patrons with both scholarly and geopolitical aims (the Great Game), and mentions Semenov-Tian-Shanskii's earlier undertakings only in passing; the reviewer notes that the book's authors distance themselves from the debates on the imperial dimension. Used to bound the claims about patronage, not as behavioural evidence.

cross_domain_range.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_hna, src_semyonov_encspb | 1849-1910 | reference biography, art-history review, city encyclopaedia] Documented sustained work in unrelated fields with real output: botany and the Don flora (master's thesis 1851), mountain geography and glaciology, a five-volume statistical dictionary and the 1897 census, a 700,000-specimen insect collection (DSB), headship of the Russian Entomological Society 1890-1914 (encspb), and a 700-picture Dutch painting collection with a published 1906 catalogue and an expert's friendships with Bode and Bredius (HNA). Three independent source types agree on the breadth; none is critical.

independent_thinking.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_krsu | 1856-1857 | reference biography, scholarly article] The DSB says his annotations corrected Ritter and Humboldt and that his Tien Shan route refuted Humboldt's volcanic origin of the mountains and the Chu-Issyk-Kul link; the 2026 KRSU article repeats the volcanic and Chu findings from the Society's own report. Two documented corrections of the two leading authorities he had trained under, both from admiring sources and the second derived from the first line of tradition, so only a moderate score.

mastery_orientation.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_hna | 1853-1910 | reference biography, art-history review] Before the expedition he spent 1853-55 in Berlin attending university lectures in geography and geology, walking in the Alps and making seventeen ascents of Vesuvius (DSB); decades later he built connoisseur-level expertise in Dutch painting, catalogued his own collection in 1906 and published the Etudes volume (HNA). Two separate fields in which he trained or studied deliberately; the Berlin account comes from one reference entry. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): lowered from 74 / 0.60 to 72 / 0.55 because the preparation story rests on a single reference-work entry and the art expertise is reported by one reviewer.

planning_orientation.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_krsu, src_semyonov_encspb | 1853-1897 | reference biography, scholarly article, city encyclopaedia] He prepared for the Tien Shan journey over roughly two years of study in Berlin (DSB), selected an expedition artist for a defined documentary role and later praised his work (KRSU), and as statistics chief organised the First All-Russian Statistical Congress (1870) and initiated the 1897 census (DSB, encspb). Multi-step, long-horizon organisation documented in three sources, though none narrates his planning method directly.

persistence.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_encspb, src_semyonov_moscow | 1856-1896 | reference biography, city encyclopaedia, municipal page] Long projects carried across decades: the five-volume translation and supplement of Ritter's Asia volumes (1856-1879), the five-volume Geographical-Statistical Dictionary (1863-1885), the three-volume history of the Russian Geographical Society (1896) and four decades as the Society's vice-president (1873-1914). Publication dates are consistent across the three sources; they speak to sustained output rather than to overcoming a named setback.

collaboration.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_ebsco, src_semyonov_krsu | 1856-1888 | reference biography, encyclopedic overview, scholarly article] The DSB lists the expeditions he organised for Przhevalsky, Pevtsov, Potanin, Kozlov and Obruchev and his help to exiled scientists; the EBSCO overview confirms his backing of Przhevalsky's 1871 expedition with the War Department; the KRSU article shows him working with an expedition artist and crediting him. The overview notes Soviet-era writers inflated his share relative to Przhevalsky, so the claim is about enabling others, not about being their equal partner.

leadership_drive.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_encspb, src_semyonov_ebsco | 1860-1914 | reference biography, city encyclopaedia, encyclopedic overview] Scientific-institution leadership held for decades: president of the Section of Physical Geography from 1860, head of the Central Statistical Committee from 1864, vice-president of the Russian Geographical Society 1873-1914 and head of the Russian Entomological Society 1890-1914. Only the scientific and statistical offices are scored; ministerial or political roles are not. Sources list the offices but say little about how he sought or exercised them.

detail_orientation.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_hna | 1863-1910 | reference biography, art-history review] A 700,000-specimen entomological collection and a five-volume reference dictionary (DSB), plus a catalogue of his own paintings and a manuscript supplement in 1910 (HNA). The outputs imply meticulousness, but no source describes his working method, so this is an inference from the scale of cataloguing work.

impact_motivation.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_hna, src_semyonov_ebsco | 1856-1910 | reference biography, art-history review, encyclopedic overview] He wrote, edited and organised popular and statistical works (Picturesque Russia, the census, the Society's history), is reported to have held that accurate geographical knowledge and a census were keys to a modern state (EBSCO summary), and in 1910 offered his whole picture collection to the Hermitage at half its appraised value so that it would stay together in St Petersburg (HNA). Motive is read from outcomes and one summarised statement, so confidence is below 0.5.

curiosity.rationale: [src_semyonov_dsb, src_semyonov_krsu | 1827-1857 | reference biography, scholarly article] The DSB records childhood interests in botany and history, geographical fieldwork on the chernozem zone at 22, and an interest in the then almost unknown Tien Shan that began while he translated Ritter; the Society's report quoted in the KRSU article lists the passes, rocks and plants he gathered in one summer. Documented exploratory interest across several decades; the childhood detail is single-source.

portrait.reason: No route met the rights bar. (1) Valentin Serov's 1905 portrait drawing of him is held by the Russian Museum (inventory R-13431, acquired from A. N. Naryshkina; the museum record opened and its identification and attribution confirmed, the drawing monogram-dated 'VS 1905'), and Serov died in 1911 so the work is old, but the museum's own terms page says that images of its collection works and the right to publish them require an official letter of request to the museum's general director, which caps the route; Commons only cites a third-party site (podol.ru) and a generic old-work tag. (2) The Alexandre Quinet photograph (1870-1889) at the Bibliotheque nationale de France, Societe de Geographie department (SG PORTRAIT-113): the Gallica record says 'restricted use (convention Societe de geographie)', which contradicts Commons' PD-BnF claim. (3) A c. 1900 photograph reproduced from the St Petersburg book 'Russia at the Paris World Exhibition of 1900' (Russian State Library record opened and the 1900 St Petersburg publication confirmed, the photographer unknown): the library viewer page that would show the caption could not be opened, so the sitter identification rests on the Commons description plus my visual similarity to the Serov drawing, and the only copy found is 267 x 331 pixels. (4) Kosharov's 1857 portrait and Koeler's 1866 portrait were found only through blog and social-media sources with no holder record. Next step: open the Russian State Library viewer page 14 of document 01003648010 in a normal browser to read the caption and, if it names Semenov, use that photograph; or obtain the Russian Museum's written permission for the Serov drawing.

CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Dictionary of Scientific Biography entry on Semyonov-Tyan-Shansky, as reproduced by Encyclopedia.com (https://encyclopedia.com/science/dictionaries-thesauruses-pictures-and-press-releases/semyonov-tyan-shansky-petr-petrovich). READ (7 sources besides Wikidata): DSB entry (full); KRSU 2026 scholarly article (full PDF); HNA review of Sokolova's monograph (full); EBSCO Research Starters on Przhevalsky (summarising fetch tool only); Saint Petersburg Encyclopaedia entry; Moscow municipal page; Ab Imperio review (context). Wikipedia was not used as support. PERSPECTIVES: (1) scientific reference biography (DSB); (2) recent regional scholarly article centred on the expedition artist; (3) independent art-history review of a Hermitage curator's monograph; (4) Przhevalsky-side encyclopedic overview that notes Soviet-era over-crediting of Semenov; (5) city commemorative pages; (6) historiographic review on the imperial and geopolitical framing of Inner Asian exploration. NON-SELF BEHAVIOURAL SOURCES: DSB, KRSU article, HNA review, EBSCO overview. SELF MATERIAL: his letters and memoirs appear only as quotations in the KRSU article and are never the sole support for a row. CONTRADICTIONS AND LIMITS: DSB says the painting collection was presented to the Hermitage in 1910, whereas the HNA review says he offered it at half its appraised value and it passed to the Hermitage after his death in 1914 (the review is followed); DSB gives the 1906 'Tyan-Shansky' addition as the 'fifteenth' and elsewhere the 'fiftieth' anniversary of the 1856 expedition (the decree date 23 November 1906 and the 1856-57 expedition imply fifty years); offices differ by source (Central Statistical Committee head 1864-73 or 1864-74; 'head' versus 'vice-president' of the Russian Geographical Society, the vice-president wording is used). No adversarial biography was found; the Ab Imperio review and the EBSCO note on Soviet-era over-crediting are the only critical framings. NOT OPENED: the Hakluyt Society edition of his Travels in the Tian'-Shan' (1998) and its introduction, the 1991 Kozlov biography, Berg's chapter, his memoirs, the Prlib page (blocked). MAJOR ACHIEVEMENT GATE (first pass): cards (1) Tien Shan expedition, (2) Russian Geographical Society and Inner Asian expeditions, (3) statistics, dictionary and census; the Dutch painting collection and the entomological collection are left out as secondary and mentioned in the editorial review notes. SELF-CALIBRATION: reviewed mastery_orientation (lowered 74/0.60 to 72/0.55), persistence and cross_domain_range (kept). No broad scoring problem flagged; the whole profile rests on admiring reference and regional sources with no adversarial biography, so confidence stays at or below 0.62.
